name: acad-mesh
description:
AutoCAD MESHES - cages of flat faces that AutoCAD can round off by subdividing. A mesh is neither a solid nor a surface, and the difference decides when to reach for one: solids are for engineered shapes where dimensions matter, meshes are for organic and sculpted ones where the form is pushed about until it looks right. Smoothing is reversible, because the underlying cage is kept.

Covers creating mesh primitives, reading a mesh's vertex and face counts and its current smoothness, raising and lowering that smoothness (MESHSMOOTHMORE and MESHSMOOTHLESS), and converting a mesh into a solid or a surface (CONVTOSOLID, CONVTOSURFACE).

Two things this category cannot do, which are facts about the AutoCAD .NET API rather than gaps here. A mesh carries NO volume, NO surface area and NO watertight flag - SubDMesh exposes none of them - so measuring a mesh means converting it to a solid, and that conversion succeeding is itself the proof the cage was watertight. And there are no factory methods for mesh primitives at all, unlike Solid3d which has a full set; every primitive here is tessellated by hand from SetSubDMesh, which is why the vertex and face counts are known before the call and checked against what comes back.

Does NOT cover: solids, which are acad-geometry-3d; surfaces, which are acad-surfaces; boolean operations, which are acad-boolean-ops. Requires the plugin.

tools_summary.name: convert_mesh_to_solid
tools_summary.description: Turn a mesh into a 3D SOLID - AutoCAD's CONVTOSOLID. This only works on a WATERTIGHT cage, where every edge is shared by exactly two faces; a mesh with a hole in it, or with faces wound inconsistently, encloses nothing and is refused. Because SubDMesh has no volume of its own, this is the only way to measure a mesh, and an unsmoothed box mesh converting to exactly its side cubed is the proof the cage was built and wound correctly. Pass smooth true to have AutoCAD fit curved faces to the facets rather than keeping them flat - the volume then differs, because the shape does.
intent: convert a mesh to a solid
make a solid out of this mesh
measure the volume of a mesh
turn a watertight mesh into a solid

tools_summary.name: convert_mesh_to_surface
tools_summary.description: Turn a mesh into a SURFACE - AutoCAD's CONVTOSURFACE. Unlike convert_mesh_to_solid this works on ANY mesh, watertight or not, because a surface is a shell that never had to enclose anything: a torn cage the solid conversion refuses converts to a surface perfectly well. Pass smooth true to fit curved faces to the facets rather than keeping them flat. Use surfaces.get_surface_info to measure what comes out.

make a surface out of this mesh
convert an open mesh that will not become a solid

tools_summary.name: create_mesh_box
tools_summary.description: Create a mesh BOX from two opposite corners - the mesh counterpart of geometry_3d.draw_box. A mesh is a cage of flat faces that AutoCAD can round off by subdividing, which is what you want for organic or sculpted shapes rather than engineered ones. smoothLevel 0 leaves it sharp and each level after that rounds it further, towards a ball. The cage stays 8 vertices and 6 faces at every level - AutoCAD reports the cage, not the subdivision - and those counts are checked against what came back, because there is no CreateBox for meshes in the AutoCAD API: the cage is written out by hand here, so the numbers are known before the call.
intent: box as a mesh not a solid

tools_summary.name: get_mesh_info
tools_summary.description: Report a mesh's vertex count, face count, current smoothness and bounding box. Read-only. Note what is NOT here and cannot be: a mesh has no volume and no surface area, because SubDMesh exposes neither - to measure one you convert it with convert_mesh_to_solid, which is itself the check on whether the cage is watertight. The counts, by contrast, are exact, and they are how you tell what smoothing has done to a mesh.
intent: how many faces does this mesh have

tools_summary.name: set_mesh_smoothness
tools_summary.description: Raise or lower how much AutoCAD rounds a mesh off - MESHSMOOTHMORE and MESHSMOOTHLESS. Give either `level`, the smoothness to set from 0 to 4, or `by`, a step from where it is now: by 1 is smooth-more and by -1 is smooth-less. Note what the face count does NOT do: it does not multiply. AutoCAD reports the CAGE - a box mesh answers 6 faces at every level - not the subdivided surface, so the count cannot tell you whether smoothing took. What changes is the SHAPE: subdividing pulls the corners in and the mesh shrinks inside its own cage, and that is what the tool measures before reporting success. Smoothing is REVERSIBLE because the cage is kept, so coming back down returns the original mesh rather than an approximation of it.
